# Data Reader

## Description

`DATA_READER` is a flexible flat-file reader (formerly `UniversalDataReader`, later `FlatFileReader`). It parses delimited / fixed-length text into records using metadata defined on its output port, and supports the line-by-line and port-reading patterns needed for non-uniform or complex files (header/footer blocks, mixed field counts, content-dependent data boundaries).

> **Name vs type:** the canonical type string is `DATA_READER`. `UniversalDataReader` is a legacy alias — never emit it in generated XML.

## Purpose & when to use

Reach for DATA_READER when:
- You need fine-grained control over flat-file parsing (delimiter overrides, skip semantics, controlled error routing, port reading).
- The file is non-uniform — title/metadata header block, footer block, or rows with different field counts/delimiters — and standard parsing can't handle it (use the line-by-line pattern).
- You want to read raw lines and classify/route them downstream before parsing.

Don't use DATA_READER when:
- The file is a clean, uniform CSV / TSV / pipe-delimited file → `csv-file` (FLAT_FILE_READER) is simpler.
- The source is a CloverDX-native binary file → use `cdx-file` (CLOVER_READER, schema auto-propagates).
- The source is Excel / JSON / XML → use `spreadsheet-reader` / `json-extract` / `xml-extract`.

## XML template

```xml
<Node enabled="enabled" fileURL="${DATAIN_DIR}/input.csv" guiName="Read CSV"
      guiX="25" guiY="150" id="DATA_READER0" type="DATA_READER">
    <attr name="charset"><![CDATA[UTF-8]]></attr>
</Node>
```

- `type="DATA_READER"`.
- Mandatory attribute: `fileURL`.
- All attributes go as `<attr name="..."><![CDATA[...]]></attr>` children.
- No CTL2 — DATA_READER is fully declarative (no `transform`/CTL anchor). Parsing is driven by node attributes + the output-port metadata.

Output-port metadata is part of the contract; declare delimiters on the `<Record>`, not on individual fields:

```xml
<Record fieldDelimiter=";" name="data" recordDelimiter="\n" type="delimited">
  <Field name="col1" type="string"/>
  <Field name="col2" type="string"/>
  <Field name="col3" type="string"/>
</Record>
```

## Properties

Parsing is always a **combination** of the node's own attributes and the metadata on output port 0. Getting the metadata right is a prerequisite — misconfigured metadata is the most common cause of parse failures.

| Attr | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fileURL` | required | See `### File URL formats`. |
| `charset` | UTF-8 | Encoding of input file — always specify explicitly. |
| `dataPolicy` | `strict` | See `### Data policy`. |
| `skipFirstLine` | false | **Deprecated.** Legacy one-line header skip; prefer `skipRows="1"` or explicit preprocessing. |
| `skipRows` | 0 | Records to skip from start of source before conversion to target field types. See `### skipRows semantics`. |
| `skipSourceRows` | 0 | Lines to skip per source file (multiple files). |
| `numRecords` | unlimited | Max records to read total. |
| `numSourceRecords` | unlimited | Max records per source file. |
| `trim` | false (unset) | Strip leading/trailing whitespace from string fields. See `### Trim strings`. |
| `quotedStrings` | (from metadata) | Enable quoted field parsing. |
| `quoteCharacter` | (from metadata) | `"` or `'`. |
| `missingColumnHandling` | treat as error | `fill_with_null` to accept short records. |
| `maxErrorCount` | unlimited | Max errors before abort (controlled mode). |
| `treatMultipleDelimitersAsOne` | false | Collapse consecutive delimiters. |
| `incrementalFile` | — | Path to incremental state file (pair with `incrementalKey`). |
| `incrementalKey` | — | Field name tracking last read position. |
| `parser` | `auto` | Underlying flat-file parser. See `### Data parsers`. |
| `verbose` | false | Richer parse diagnostics (record/field context + problematic values) at slight performance cost. See `### verbose mode`. |

### Metadata design — set delimiters on `<Record>`, not on individual fields

Set `fieldDelimiter` and `recordDelimiter` on the `<Record>` element. Only override per-field when a specific field truly uses a different delimiter (rare — typically only the last field might need `eofAsDelimiter="true"`).

```xml
<!-- WRONG — verbose, redundant, brittle -->
<Record name="data" type="delimited">
  <Field name="col1" type="string" delimiter=";"/>
  <Field name="col2" type="string" delimiter=";"/>
  <Field name="col3" type="string" delimiter="\n"/>
</Record>

<!-- CORRECT — clean and idiomatic -->
<Record fieldDelimiter=";" name="data" recordDelimiter="\n" type="delimited">
  <Field name="col1" type="string"/>
  <Field name="col2" type="string"/>
  <Field name="col3" type="string"/>
</Record>
```

Putting explicit `delimiter="..."` on every field is not how CloverDX delimited metadata is idiomatically written. It is redundant, increases the chance of inconsistency, and is fragile when fields are reordered.

**Always verify the actual delimiter before defining metadata.** Read a sample of the source file first. Do not assume `,` — many real-world CSV exports use `;`, `|`, or `\t`. A mismatch between the declared `fieldDelimiter` and the file's actual separator causes the parser to treat each entire row as a single field, producing single-field records with no error (if `lenient`) or an immediate parse failure (if `strict`).

### Data policy

`dataPolicy` controls what happens when a record cannot be parsed according to the metadata.

| Value | Behaviour | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `strict` | Fail immediately on first parse error | Default; use during development and for trusted well-structured files |
| `controlled` | Route bad records to port 1; continue processing | Need to capture and inspect rejected rows; port 1 must be connected |
| `lenient` | Silently discard bad records; continue | **Avoid** — produces zero output with no error message when the whole file is rejected; hides real problems |

**Never use `lenient` as a workaround for a file that is hard to parse.** If parsing fails, the correct approach is to diagnose using `strict`, understand why records fail, then either fix the metadata or switch to the line-by-line reading pattern.

**`controlled` requires port 1 to be connected** — to TRASH or a writer. If port 1 has no edge, the component raises an init-time error. Port 1 metadata must match the exact 5-field error schema (see `## Input & output metadata` → `### Error port metadata`) — connecting regular record metadata to port 1 causes a component initialization failure.

### `skipRows` semantics

`skipRows` means the number of source records/rows to skip from the input source(s) (see CloverDX "Selecting input records").

Important: this does **not** mean the line is ignored before parsing. DATA_READER still has to split the input text according to delimiters and record structure. Only mapping/conversion of values to target field types is skipped for those rows.

Therefore, if splitting itself fails (for example because of missing delimiters, broken quoting, malformed row structure), the component can still fail even when `skipRows` is set.

If certain lines must be truly ignored regardless of parseability, use the line-by-line pattern (see `## Examples` → `### Full — line-by-line reading`): read whole lines first, filter/classify lines downstream (e.g. in REFORMAT), then parse only filtered rows in a subsequent component.

### Trim strings — exact hierarchy

Three attributes interact when deciding whether leading/trailing whitespace is stripped:

1. **`trim` (default = unset).** Unset behaves type-dependently:
   - For numeric / boolean / date fields, leading and trailing whitespace is **stripped before parsing** regardless of the attribute. Numeric parsing cannot tolerate embedded whitespace, so this is forced.
   - For `string` / `byte` / `cbyte` fields, whitespace is **preserved** by default — the field receives raw bytes including spaces.
2. **`trim="true"`.** Strips both ends for **all** field types. A field of only whitespace becomes a zero-length string (note: zero-length, not null).
3. **`trim="false"`.** Preserves whitespace for all field types — including numeric. **Numeric parsing then fails on padded values** (e.g. `"   42"` raises a parse error). Use carefully.
4. **`skipLeadingBlanks` / `skipTrailingBlanks`** (advanced) — override `trim` per side. Set explicitly (`true` / `false`) to win over `trim`. If both are at their default, `trim` decides.

Practical rule: leave `trim` unset (default) for mixed numeric + string metadata. Set `trim="true"` only when string fields legitimately need both-sides stripping.

### Data parsers

`parser` selects the underlying flat-file parser. Default `auto` is correct in 95% of cases — set explicitly only when you need the trade-off:

| Parser | When chosen | Restrictions |
|---|---|---|
| `org.jetel.data.parser.SimpleDataParser` | Pure-delimited records, no advanced features | **Ignored attributes:** `trim` / `skipLeadingBlanks` / `skipTrailingBlanks` / `incrementalFile` / `incrementalKey` / `skipRows` / `numRecords` / `quotedStrings` / `missingColumnHandling` / `treatMultipleDelimitersAsOne` / `verbose`. **Ignored field options:** fixed-length fields, no-delimiter or multi-delimiter fields, `Shift` non-null, `Autofilling`, byte-based fields. Fastest but most restricted. |
| `org.jetel.data.parser.DataParser` | Default fallback covering all attributes | All attributes work. Slightly slower than SimpleDataParser. |
| `org.jetel.data.parser.CharByteDataParser` | Metadata mixes byte (`byte` / `cbyte` / `BINARY:` format) and char-based fields | Required when binary + text fields coexist. |
| `org.jetel.data.parser.FixLenByteDataParser` | All fields are byte-based, fixed length | Specialized binary; use only when all fields are bytes. |

**Auto-selection logic:** `auto` picks `SimpleDataParser` when no advanced feature is in use, otherwise `DataParser`. Picking `SimpleDataParser` explicitly while also using `quotedStrings="true"` silently ignores the quoting (common gotcha).

### `verbose` mode — when to turn it on

Use `verbose=true` primarily for troubleshooting, especially when DATA_READER starts failing on data quality or parsing issues and the default error message is too generic.

- Default (`verbose=false`): less detailed error notifications, slightly better performance.
- Troubleshooting (`verbose=true`): more detailed diagnostic output, slightly lower performance.

Practical guidance:
- Keep `verbose=false` for normal production runs when parsing is stable.
- Switch to `verbose=true` during investigation of parse failures (wrong delimiter, malformed quoting, inconsistent field counts, bad numeric/date conversions, etc.).
- After root cause is identified and fixed, switch back to `verbose=false` if you need maximum throughput.

### File URL formats

```
${DATAIN_DIR}/input.csv                          local file
${DATAIN_DIR}/data/*.csv                         glob wildcard — reads all matching files
${DATAIN_DIR}/data/file1.csv;file2.csv           semicolon-separated list
zip:(${DATAIN_DIR}/archive.zip)!data/input.csv   single file from ZIP
zip:(${DATAIN_DIR}/archive.zip)!*.csv            all CSVs from ZIP
port:$0.fieldName:discrete                       each port record = one complete "file"
port:$0.fieldName:stream                         all port records concatenated = one stream
port:$0.filePath:source                          port field contains a file path to open
dict:myDictEntry                                 read from dictionary entry
http://example.com/data.csv                      remote HTTP
ftp://user:pass@host/path/file.csv               remote FTP
```

### Autofilling fields on output metadata

Add `auto_filling` to a `<Field>` in port 0 metadata to have DATA_READER inject a pre-defined value automatically at read time. The value is filled only at the output port of the reader — no other component can provide it.

```xml
<Field auto_filling="source_name"      name="fileName"   type="string"/>
<Field auto_filling="global_row_count" name="rowNum"     type="integer"/>
<Field auto_filling="row_timestamp"    name="loadedAt"   type="date" format="yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"/>
```

| Function | Field type | Fills with |
|---|---|---|
| `default_value` | any | The field's `default` property value when nothing is read |
| `global_row_count` | numeric | Sequential record number across all sources (starts at 0, continuous) |
| `global_row_incl_err_count` | numeric | Same, including error records |
| `source_row_count` | numeric | Record number per source (resets to 0 for each new source) |
| `source_row_incl_err_count` | numeric | Same, including error records |
| `metadata_row_count` | numeric | Row count scoped to edges sharing the same metadata, continuous across sources |
| `metadata_source_row_count` | numeric | Same scope, resets per source |
| `source_name` | string | Name/path of the data source being read |
| `source_timestamp` | date | Timestamp of the data source ¹ |
| `source_size` | numeric | Size of the data source ¹ |
| `row_timestamp` | date | Time when the individual record is read |
| `reader_timestamp` | date | Time when the reader starts (same for all records in the run) |

¹ **`source_timestamp` and `source_size` work only for direct local/remote file reads.** For archive sources (`zip:(...)!`, `tar:(...)!`) `source_timestamp` is empty and `source_size` is `0`. Do not rely on these for archive-sourced ingestion.

## Input & output metadata

You define the metadata on the data ports — parsing is driven by output port 0's metadata together with the node attributes. Only the error/log port (port 1) has an engine default, and it is **structure-enforced**: exactly the 5 fields below, in order, types fixed, names arbitrary (see `### Error port metadata`).

```
auto_propagated_metadata:   # mixed — you define the data ports; the logs port is structure-enforced
  in.0:  <you define — port-reading source>    # optional; the raw-data field must be string | byte | cbyte
  out.0: <you define — parsed record schema>   # required; metadata + node attributes drive parsing
  out.1: UniversalDataReader_Error             # logs port (dataPolicy=controlled) — exactly these 5 fields, in order
    recordNo:long  fieldNo:integer  originalData:string  errorMessage:string  fileURL:string
```

Edges on the data ports reference your `<Metadata>` explicitly (see `### Edge declarations`); on port 1 use the offered `UniversalDataReader_Error` template or any `<Metadata>` matching the enforced structure — anything else fails initialization.

### Port reading (general)

DATA_READER can read from an upstream port field instead of a file:

```
port:$0.fieldName:discrete   field contains full file content; one "file" per record
port:$0.fieldName:stream     all records form one stream treated as one file
port:$0.filePath:source      field contains a file path; reader opens that file
```

Input port 0 field type must be `string`, `byte`, or `cbyte`.

### Error port metadata (port 1, controlled mode)

Exactly 5 fields in this order — no other structure is accepted:

| # | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `long` | Record position (1-based) |
| 1 | `integer` | Field position (1-based) |
| 2 | `string`/`byte`/`cbyte` | Raw erroneous record |
| 3 | `string`/`byte`/`cbyte` | Error message |
| 4 | `string` | Source file URL |

Connecting any other metadata to port 1 (e.g. the same record metadata as port 0) causes: `The log port metadata has invalid format` at initialization — the graph will not start.

### Edge declarations

```xml
<!-- Standard -->
<Edge fromNode="DATA_READER0:0" id="E0" inPort="Port 0 (in)"    metadata="MyMeta"    outPort="Port 0 (output)" toNode="NEXT:0"/>
<!-- Error port (controlled mode) -->
<Edge fromNode="DATA_READER0:1" id="E1" inPort="Port 0 (in)"    metadata="ErrorMeta" outPort="Port 1 (output)" toNode="TRASH0:0"/>
<!-- Port reading input -->
<Edge fromNode="UPSTREAM:0"     id="E2" inPort="Port 0 (input)" metadata="LineMeta"  outPort="Port 0 (out)"    toNode="DATA_READER1:0"/>
```

Note: the input port on DATA_READER uses `inPort="Port 0 (input)"`, **not** `Port 0 (in)`.

## Examples

### Minimal — read a delimited file

```xml
<Metadata id="MyMeta">
  <Record fieldDelimiter=";" name="data" recordDelimiter="\n" type="delimited">
    <Field name="col1" type="string"/>
    <Field name="col2" type="string"/>
    <Field name="col3" type="string"/>
  </Record>
</Metadata>

<Node enabled="enabled" fileURL="${DATAIN_DIR}/input.csv" guiName="Read CSV"
      guiX="25" guiY="150" id="DATA_READER0" type="DATA_READER">
    <attr name="charset"><![CDATA[UTF-8]]></attr>
</Node>
```

### Full — line-by-line reading (non-uniform / complex files)

**When to use:** the file structure is non-uniform and standard parsing cannot work —

- File has a title/metadata header block before the data rows (variable or fixed length).
- File has a footer block (totals, summaries) after data rows.
- Header, data, and footer rows have different field counts or different delimiters.
- `skipRows` cannot solve it because the data section boundary is content-dependent.
- `dataPolicy="lenient"` produces zero output — the parser is rejecting all rows silently.

**Strategy:** Use DATA_READER with single-field line metadata to slurp the file one raw line at a time with zero parsing. Every line — blanks, title, column header, data rows, footer — arrives as a plain string. Downstream logic classifies and routes.

`LineMeta` — the correct single-field metadata:

```xml
<Metadata id="LineMeta">
    <Record name="raw_line" type="delimited" charset="UTF-8">
        <Field name="line" type="string" delimiter="\n|\r\n|\r" eofAsDelimiter="true"/>
    </Record>
</Metadata>
```

Critical rules for `LineMeta`:
- No `recordDelimiter` on `<Record>` — the field delimiter alone drives record boundaries.
- `delimiter="\n|\r\n|\r"` on the field — pipe-separated alternatives handle Unix (`\n`), Windows (`\r\n`), and old Mac (`\r`) line endings.
- `eofAsDelimiter="true"` on the field — the last line of a file typically has no trailing newline; without this the parser hits EOF before finding the delimiter and fails with `Unexpected end of file in record N, field 1`.
- Do NOT set `recordDelimiter="\n"` and `fieldDelimiter="\n"` simultaneously — the parser becomes ambiguous and fails with `Unexpected default field delimiter`.
- Do NOT set `delimiter` to a character that appears in the data (e.g. `;` for CSV files).

DATA_READER node — no `skipRows`, no `dataPolicy`:
```xml
<Node enabled="enabled" fileURL="${DATAIN_DIR}/export.csv" guiName="Read Lines"
      guiX="25" guiY="150" id="DATA_READER0" type="DATA_READER">
    <attr name="charset"><![CDATA[UTF-8]]></attr>
</Node>
```

#### Option A — REFORMAT with CTL (parse in-place)

REFORMAT receives each raw line, classifies it, splits on the delimiter, and maps fields by index to the output metadata. No extra component needed. Best when field parsing logic is manageable in CTL.

```xml
<Node enabled="enabled" guiName="Filter + Parse" guiX="300" guiY="150"
      id="REFORMAT0" type="REFORMAT">
    <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    string line = $in.0.line;
    if (isnull(line) || length(trim(line)) == 0) { return SKIP; }
    list[string] parts = split(line, ";");
    if (length(parts) < 13) { return SKIP; }          // header/footer rows have fewer fields
    if (!contains(parts[12], "ExpectedMarker")) { return SKIP; }
    $out.0.Symbol = trim(parts[2]);
    $out.0.Amount = str2double(replace(replace(parts[4], " ", ""), ",", "."));
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>
</Node>
```

#### Option B — Filter REFORMAT + port-reading second DATA_READER

REFORMAT acts as a lightweight line classifier only — drops blanks and structural garbage, passes qualifying raw lines. A second DATA_READER reads those lines via port and parses them using the full target metadata. Best when data rows are well-structured but the surrounding file is not.

```xml
<!-- Stage 1: read all lines raw -->
<Node enabled="enabled" fileURL="${DATAIN_DIR}/export.csv" guiName="Read Lines"
      guiX="25" guiY="150" id="DATA_READER0" type="DATA_READER">
    <attr name="charset"><![CDATA[UTF-8]]></attr>
</Node>

<!-- Stage 2: lightweight classifier — drop blanks and lines without a delimiter -->
<Node enabled="enabled" guiName="Filter Structured Lines" guiX="275" guiY="150"
      id="REFORMAT0" type="REFORMAT">
    <attr name="transform"><![CDATA[//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    string line = $in.0.line;
    if (isnull(line) || length(trim(line)) == 0) { return SKIP; }
    if (!contains(line, ";")) { return SKIP; }   // plain-text header lines have no semicolons
    $out.0.line = line;
    return ALL;
}
]]></attr>
</Node>

<!-- Stage 3: parse filtered lines — each line is one discrete "file" -->
<Node enabled="enabled" fileURL="port:$0.line:discrete" guiName="Parse Data Lines"
      guiX="550" guiY="150" id="DATA_READER1" type="DATA_READER">
    <attr name="charset"><![CDATA[UTF-8]]></attr>
    <attr name="dataPolicy"><![CDATA[strict]]></attr>
</Node>

<Edge fromNode="DATA_READER0:0" id="E0" inPort="Port 0 (in)"    metadata="LineMeta"   outPort="Port 0 (output)" toNode="REFORMAT0:0"/>
<Edge fromNode="REFORMAT0:0"    id="E1" inPort="Port 0 (input)" metadata="LineMeta"   outPort="Port 0 (out)"    toNode="DATA_READER1:0"/>
<Edge fromNode="DATA_READER1:0" id="E2" inPort="Port 0 (in)"    metadata="ParsedMeta" outPort="Port 0 (output)" toNode="NEXT:0"/>
```

Option B specific rules:
- Edge to DATA_READER1 input uses `inPort="Port 0 (input)"` (not `Port 0 (in)`).
- `port:$0.fieldName:discrete` — each record from the port = one complete "file" to parse. Use for line-by-line (one parsed record per line).
- `port:$0.fieldName:stream` — all records concatenated = one file stream. Use when multiple port records together form a single logical file.
- **Last field in `ParsedMeta` must have `eofAsDelimiter="true"`** — each line arrives without a trailing newline, so the parser hits EOF before finding the last field's `\n` delimiter. Without this, DATA_READER1 fails with `Unexpected end of file in record 1, field N`. Example: `<Field name="Trailing" type="string" delimiter="\n" eofAsDelimiter="true"/>`.
- Use `dataPolicy="strict"` on DATA_READER1 — do not use `lenient` (hides parse failures silently). Any rows that slip through REFORMAT0 and fail to parse (e.g. column header, footer) will error clearly, allowing diagnosis and fix.
- Do NOT connect port 1 on DATA_READER1 unless you have the correct 5-field error metadata — wrong metadata on port 1 causes a component initialization failure before the graph runs.

## Common mistakes

| Wrong | Correct |
|---|---|
| `type="UniversalDataReader"` | `type="DATA_READER"` |
| `dataPolicy="lenient"` to handle a hard-to-parse file | Produces zero output silently — use `strict`, diagnose from log, fix root cause or switch to line-by-line |
| `fieldDelimiter="\n"` and `recordDelimiter="\n"` both set on LineMeta | `recordDelimiter=""` (empty) + `fieldDelimiter="\n"` |
| `fieldDelimiter` set to `;` or other data character in LineMeta | Use `\n` as field delimiter; never a character that appears in the data |
| `skipRows` to skip non-uniform header blocks | Only works when header is a fixed line count AND all data rows share the same structure; use line-by-line + REFORMAT for mixed files |
| Omitting `charset` | Always specify; default varies by system and JVM locale |
| `dataPolicy="controlled"` with no edge on port 1 | Port 1 must be connected (to TRASH or a writer) |
| Connecting regular record metadata to port 1 | Port 1 requires the exact 5-field error schema — wrong metadata causes init-time failure |
| `fileURL="port:$0.line:discrete"` without `eofAsDelimiter="true"` on last field | Parser hits EOF before finding the last field delimiter — add `eofAsDelimiter="true"` to the last field in the target metadata |
| `inPort="Port 0 (in)"` on DATA_READER port-reading input edge | Use `inPort="Port 0 (input)"` for the DATA_READER input port |
| `dataPolicy="lenient"` on the port-reading DATA_READER1 | Use `strict` — lenient silently drops rows that fail, hiding real parsing problems |
| Multiple source files with `skipRows` | Use `skipSourceRows` to skip header per file; `skipRows` skips only from the first source |

## Notes

### Compatibility / version history

| Version | Change |
|---|---|
| 4.2.0-M1 | Component renamed `UniversalDataReader` → `FlatFileReader` (XML type still `DATA_READER`). |
| 4.4.0-M2 | Default charset changed from `ISO-8859-1` to `UTF-8`. Always specify `charset` explicitly to remain stable across versions. |
| 6.0.0 | UTF BOM bytes are stripped from the data when any UTF charset is used — including when reading into a `byte` field. Pre-6.0 graphs that explicitly stripped BOMs downstream should remove that step. |

### Iterative debug approach

When parsing fails or produces unexpected record counts, iterate using `strict` mode:

1. **Set `dataPolicy="strict"`** — graph fails on the first bad record with a specific error message identifying field name, record number, and the problem.
2. **Read the execution log** — look for `Parsing error:` lines. They name the field, record number, and the value that failed.
3. **Fix the root cause** — wrong delimiter, wrong field count in metadata, missing `eofAsDelimiter`, wrong charset, etc.
4. **Re-run and repeat** — `strict` stops at the first error each time; multiple issues may require multiple iterations.
5. **Switch to `controlled`** only after `strict` succeeds cleanly, if you need ongoing error handling for genuinely dirty production data.

Common error messages and their fixes:

| Error message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Unexpected default field delimiter, probably record has too many fields` | `fieldDelimiter` matches a character that appears in the data | Change `fieldDelimiter` in metadata to a character not present in the data |
| `Unexpected end of file in record N, field M ("fieldName")` | Last field delimiter not found — EOF reached before the expected record terminator | Set `eofAsDelimiter="true"` on the last field, or ensure `recordDelimiter` matches actual line endings |
| `The log port metadata has invalid format` | Port 1 connected with wrong metadata | Port 1 requires the exact 5-field error schema (see `## Input & output metadata` → `### Error port metadata`) |
| `Component initialization failed` | Port 1 connected but metadata wrong, or `dataPolicy="controlled"` with no port 1 edge | Fix port 1 metadata or connect the edge |
